description: USG Funding Department rules: deadlines, caps, eligible and ineligible expenses, required documents and the four funds.

rules.title: How academic weeks are counted
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Review the Funding Application Deadlines to see the event dates that are eligible for funding and the submission deadline for the application.
rules.verification_note: USG's guidelines do not say how academic weeks are counted. Its deadline table needs a USC sign-in, and Greenlight's copy of it has not been confirmed. Check the date in USG's Funding Application Deadlines table or with usgfunds@usc.edu.
rules.message: USG deadlines are counted in academic weeks, but the guidelines do not define an academic week. They point to USG's Funding Application Deadlines table.
rules.fix_template: Check the date in USG's Funding Application Deadlines table or ask USG (usgfunds@usc.edu).
rules.applies_to: Every USG deadline counted in academic weeks
rules.notes: Open question in PROJECT_CONTEXT section 8. A hand transcription of the table, made in a signed-in browser on 2026-11-14, is in rules/sources/usg-funding-deadlines.txt; code cannot check it against the sheet. The transcribed table is keyed by event week and gives a 6-week and a 9-week deadline (always a Wednesday). It does not follow a simple count of weeks, so deadlines should be looked up in it, not computed. Weeks with no deadline (winter recess, study days, finals, spring recess) have no USG funding.

rules.title: USG application deadline for approved-vendor purchases
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Applications must be submitted at least six academic weeks six academic weeks before the initial payment due date, for approved USC Vendors.
rules.message: Apply to USG at least 6 academic weeks before the first payment to the vendor is due. A late application is denied automatically.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, or move the payment due date (and the event) later.
rules.applies_to: Any USG application that pays an approved USC vendor
rules.check: application_date <= initial_payment_due_date - 6 academic weeks
rules.notes: The sentence in the guidelines repeats the words 'six academic weeks'; it is quoted exactly as written. When sources give different USG deadlines, Greenlight works out each one it can and shows the earliest, citing every source.

rules.title: USG application deadline as stated on the USG web page
rules.source: USG Funding Department web page
rules.source_section: Frequently Asked Questions: When should I submit my application?
rules.source_text: Applications must be submitted on Wednesdays by 11:59 PM six academic weeks before the event date when using an approved vendor, and or nine academic weeks before the initial payment due date (whichever comes first) for approved USC Vendors.
rules.message: USG's web page says to apply 6 academic weeks before the event date, or 9 academic weeks before the first payment is due, whichever comes first. The guidelines count 6 weeks back from the first payment instead. Greenlight shows the earliest of these dates and cites both sources.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, the earliest of the deadlines.
rules.applies_to: Any USG application that pays an approved USC vendor
rules.check: application_date <= event_date - 6 academic weeks

rules.title: USG web page: 9 academic weeks before the first payment, whichever comes first
rules.source: USG Funding Department web page
rules.source_section: Frequently Asked Questions: When should I submit my application?
rules.source_text: Applications must be submitted on Wednesdays by 11:59 PM six academic weeks before the event date when using an approved vendor, and or nine academic weeks before the initial payment due date (whichever comes first) for approved USC Vendors.
rules.message: The same sentence on USG's web page also gives 9 academic weeks before the first payment due date; the earlier of the two dates applies.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, the earliest of the deadlines.
rules.applies_to: Any USG application that pays an approved USC vendor
rules.check: application_date <= initial_payment_due_date - 9 academic weeks
rules.notes: The page's sentence is garbled ('and or nine academic weeks'); it is read here as a second deadline, with 'whichever comes first' choosing between the two.

rules.title: USG application deadline for travel
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Travel expenses must be made at least 9 academic weeks prior to the date of initial payment due date. Travel expenses that require this 9 academic week deadline include transportation (airfare or ground) and hotels for an overnight stay.
rules.message: Travel (airfare, ground transport, overnight hotels) must be applied for at least 9 academic weeks before the first payment is due.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, or plan travel for a later date.
rules.applies_to: A USG application with airfare, ground transport or an overnight hotel
rules.check: application_date <= initial_payment_due_date - 9 academic weeks
rules.notes: Sources disagree: USG's FAQ document says 8 academic weeks before the event date for travel; the guidelines say 9 weeks before the first payment. When sources give different USG deadlines, Greenlight works out each one it can and shows the earliest, citing every source.

rules.title: USG FAQ: 8 academic weeks for new vendors and travel
rules.source: USG Funding FAQ document (FAQ for Funding Website)
rules.source_section: FAQ: When should I submit my application?
rules.source_text: Applications must be submitted on Wednesdays by 11:59 PM six academic weeks before the event date when using an approved vendor, and eight academic weeks before the event date for new vendors and travel.
rules.message: USG's FAQ document says 8 academic weeks before the event date for travel and for new vendors. The 2026-27 guidelines say 9 weeks before the first payment for travel, and do not accept vendors that are not on the list. Greenlight shows the earliest deadline, treats a vendor not on the list as not accepted, and cites both.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, the earlier of the deadlines.
rules.applies_to: A USG application with travel or a vendor not on the list
rules.check: application_date <= event_date - 8 academic weeks
rules.notes: The FAQ document has no date and still says 8 weeks where the 2026-27 guidelines say 9, so it may be older than the guidelines.

rules.title: A missed USG deadline means automatic denial
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Applications received within this six to nine-academic-week deadline will be reviewed by the respective Funding Director. If this deadline is not met the application will be automatically denied.
rules.message: The guidelines say an application that misses the USG deadline is denied automatically. USG's FAQ document leaves late Professional/Academic Fund travel requests to the Director's discretion; both are shown.
rules.applies_to: Every USG application

rules.title: USG FAQ: Professional Fund travel 8 weeks before the trip
rules.source: USG Funding FAQ document (FAQ for Funding Website)
rules.source_section: FAQ, Professional and Academic Fund: Why is there an 8 week deadline for travel?
rules.source_text: Travel expense requests (airfare and hotel) must be made at least eight weeks prior to the date of travel
rules.message: USG's FAQ document says Professional/Academic Fund travel requests (airfare and hotel) must be made at least 8 weeks before the travel date. The guidelines say 9 academic weeks before the first payment. Greenlight shows the earliest date and cites both.
rules.fix_template: Apply by {due_date}, the earliest of the deadlines.
rules.applies_to: A Professional/Academic Fund request with airfare or hotel

rules.title: USG FAQ: late Professional Fund travel requests are at the Director's discretion
rules.source: USG Funding FAQ document (FAQ for Funding Website)
rules.source_section: FAQ, Professional and Academic Fund: Why is there an 8 week deadline for travel?
rules.source_text: Applications received within this four week deadline, or eight week deadline in the event of air travel requests, will be considered at the discretion of the Director of the Academic Fund.
rules.message: USG's FAQ document says late Professional/Academic Fund travel requests are considered at the Director's discretion; the guidelines say a missed deadline means automatic denial.
rules.applies_to: A late Professional/Academic Fund travel request

rules.title: USG applications open on Wednesdays, first come first served
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Funding applications will be open once a week on Wednesdays and close at 11:59 PM. They will be reviewed on a first come first serve basis until all funds are exhausted. Apply as early as possible to avoid delays caused by school breaks and other technical issues.
rules.message: USG applications open once a week, on Wednesdays, and close at 11:59 PM. Money is given first come, first served until it runs out, so apply early.
rules.applies_to: Every USG application

rules.title: No USG funding for events in holidays, breaks, study days or finals
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Please be advised that USG Funding does not process applications or provide funding for events during University holidays, breaks, study days, or finals.
rules.message: USG does not fund events held during university holidays, breaks, study days or final exams, and does not process applications on those days.
rules.fix_template: Move the event out of {blocked_period_name} ({blocked_start} to {blocked_end}).
rules.applies_to: A USG-funded event whose date falls in a university holiday, break, study days or finals
rules.notes: The sentence covers both events and applications: no USG submission deadline should fall on a holiday, break, study day or finals day. The transcribed deadline table skips exactly those Wednesdays (it jumps from 2026-11-18 to 2027-01-13).

rules.title: No USG funding for summer events (USG FAQ)
rules.source: USG Funding FAQ document (FAQ for Funding Website)
rules.source_section: FAQ 6: Can I apply for summer event funding?
rules.source_text: Can I apply for summer event funding? 1. USG Funding does not process applications or provide funding for events during University holidays, breaks, study days, or finals.
rules.message: Asked whether summer events can be funded, USG's FAQ answers that it does not fund events during holidays, breaks, study days or finals. Greenlight reads this as no USG funding for events outside the fall and spring semesters; confirm with usgfunds@usc.edu.
rules.fix_template: Hold the event during the fall or spring semester, or ask USG (usgfunds@usc.edu) first.
rules.applies_to: A USG-funded event outside the fall and spring semesters (for example in summer)
rules.notes: The FAQ answers the summer question with the breaks sentence, so it implies no summer funding without saying so; shown yellow. The deadline table also has no rows after April 30, 2027.

rules.title: Post Event Evaluation form within 3 business days
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: All applicants must submit the Post Event Evaluation form found on the USG EngageSC page within three business days of the final day of the event.
rules.message: Submit USG's Post Event Evaluation form within 3 business days after the last day of the event.
rules.fix_template: Submit the Post Event Evaluation by {due_date}.
rules.applies_to: Every USG-funded event

rules.title: Post Event Evaluation needs event photos
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: This Post Event Evaluation form must include pictures of the event with members in attendance.
rules.message: The Post Event Evaluation must include photos of the event showing members attending.
rules.fix_template: Take photos during the event that show members attending.
rules.applies_to: Every USG-funded event

rules.title: Final invoices within 3 business days
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: Final invoices must be submitted no later than three business days after the final day of the event.
rules.message: Submit final invoices to USG no later than 3 business days after the last day of the event. Late invoices can lead to disciplinary action and loss of future funding.
rules.fix_template: Submit final invoices by {due_date}.
rules.applies_to: Every USG-funded event

rules.title: Complete the USG Funding Department modules

Organizations that have not gone through this process will not receive funding.
rules.message: USG funds only clubs that went through recognition with Campus Activities this year and completed the Funding Guidelines module.
rules.fix_template: Complete recognition and the USG Funding Guidelines module before applying.

rules.title: A quote for every expense
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_text: The full budget proposal for the event, including quotes for each individual expense
rules.message: Every expense needs its own quote in the budget proposal.
rules.fix_template: Get a written quote from {vendor} for {item}.
rules.applies_to: Every line of a USG budget

rules.title: Cart screenshot for online purchases

rules.source_text: For online purchases, include a screenshot of the cart showing prices, quantities, and total price including all fees.
rules.message: For an online purchase, include a screenshot of the cart showing prices, quantities and the total with all fees.

rules.title: Traveler details in the application

rules.fix_template: Name the hotel point of contact in the application.

rules.title: Statement of purpose for travel

rules.source_text: Applications requesting funding for travel expenses must include a clear statement of purpose that outlines the reasoning for the travel, including how the trip aligns with the goals/mission of the RSO or individual.

rules.title: Registration log-in details

rules.title: Fix an incomplete application within 2 business days

rules.source_text: Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant who must provide the necessary information within 2 business days .
rules.message: If USG returns the application as incomplete, the missing information must be provided within 2 business days or it is denied.
rules.fix_template: Send the missing information by {due_date}.

rules.source_section: FAQ 16: What happens if I submit an application that is missing information?
rules.source_text: If your application is missing information, the Funding Director will return it to you, and you will have three business days to provide the necessary information before your application is denied.
rules.message: USG's FAQ document says a returned application must be completed within 3 business days; the guidelines say 2 business days (48 hours). Greenlight shows the earliest of these and cites both.

rules.title: $8,000 per club per year
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 3: Maximum Funding per Academic Year
rules.source_text: Individual organizations may receive a maximum of $8,000 from the USG Funding Department per year.
rules.message: A club can receive at most $8,000 from USG in one year.
rules.fix_template: This request would bring the year's USG total to ${year_total}. Cut ${over} or fund it another way.
rules.applies_to: All USG funding to one club in one academic year
rules.check: sum(usg_funding_this_year) <= 8000

rules.title: Up to $4,000 for on-campus venue and personnel
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 3: Maximum Funding per Academic Year
rules.source_text: The USG Funding Department will provide funding for up to $4,000 of the total cost associated with on-campus venue rentals and personnel.
rules.message: USG pays at most $4,000 of the cost of on-campus venue rental and personnel.
rules.fix_template: You are asking USG for ${venue_personnel_requested} for venue and personnel. USG covers up to $4,000; ask for ${over} less and cover the rest another way.
rules.applies_to: The amount asked of USG for on-campus venue rental and personnel
rules.check: usg_requested(venue_rental + personnel) <= 4000
rules.notes: The cap limits what USG pays, not what the venue costs: a club may pay the rest itself. The guidelines do not say whether the $4,000 is per event or per year; a single request over $4,000 breaks it either way, and Phase 3 should show a total across events as needing a check.

rules.title: Events over $4,000 are reviewed case by case
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 3: Maximum Funding per Academic Year
rules.source_text: Events with expenses over $4,000 will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis to ensure effective use of funding.
rules.message: An event with expenses over $4,000 is reviewed case by case by USG. Greenlight cannot tell how USG will decide.
rules.fix_template: Contact USG (usgfunds@usc.edu) before applying.
rules.applies_to: A USG-funded event whose expenses total more than $4,000
rules.check: event_expenses_total > 4000
rules.notes: The sentence sits under the venue and personnel cap; it is read here as the event's total expenses.

rules.title: Multi-day events are reviewed case by case
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 3: Maximum Funding per Academic Year
rules.source_text: Multi-day events will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
rules.message: Multi-day events are reviewed case by case by USG.
rules.fix_template: Contact USG (usgfunds@usc.edu) before applying.

rules.title: A fund may close early in fall
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 3: Maximum Funding per Academic Year
rules.source_text: If a funding board attains a utilization rate of 50% or higher before the conclusion of the Fall semester, the Chief Financial Officer reserves the authority to withdraw said funding board from the application process and order its immediate closure until the beginning of the Spring semester application review process.
rules.message: If a fund has used 50% or more of its money before fall ends, USG may close it until spring. Apply early.

rules.title: Up to 4 funded events per semester
rules.source: USG Funding Department web page
rules.source_section: Frequently Asked Questions: How much funding is available per organization?
rules.source_text: Each RSO can have up to 4 events funded per semester as long as it remains under $8,000 from the USG Funding Department per year.
rules.verification_note: The 4-event limit is on USG's web page but not in its Funding Department Guidelines. Confirm it with usgfunds@usc.edu.
rules.message: The USG web page says a club can have up to 4 events funded per semester. This is not in the Funding Department Guidelines, so Greenlight shows it as needing confirmation.

rules.notes: Open question in PROJECT_CONTEXT section 8 ('Is the cap four funded events per semester?'). Kept yellow by the user's choice (2026-11-14).

rules.title: Reasons USG may deny an application
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 6: University Policy and Application Denials
rules.source_text: The Funding department may deny applications for a multitude of reasons, this may include, but is not limited to: * Past instances of misuse of funds within the academic year * Inappropriate contact with funding department members and/or Professional Staff within the academic year * Conflicting events requested on the same day * RSO receiving funding from another University income source * Low remaining funds due to high utilization
rules.message: USG may deny an application for reasons including misuse of funds, inappropriate contact with funding staff, conflicting events on the same day, funding from another University source, or low remaining funds. Greenlight never predicts a decision.
rules.applies_to: Every USG application

rules.title: Two funding requests on the same day
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 6: University Policy and Application Denials
rules.source_text: Conflicting events requested on the same day
rules.message: USG lists conflicting events requested on the same day as a possible reason to deny. Two of the club's funded events fall on the same day.
rules.fix_template: Move one of the events on {date} to another day, or fund only one with USG.
rules.applies_to: Two USG-funded events of one club on the same date

rules.title: Funding from another University source
rules.source: USG 26-27 Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026)
rules.source_section: Section 6: University Policy and Application Denials
rules.source_text: RSO receiving funding from another University income source
rules.message: USG lists funding from another University source as a possible reason to deny. Ask USG before combining USG money with other USC money for the same event.
rules.fix_template: Ask USG (usgfunds@usc.edu) before using {other_source} for this event.
rules.applies_to: An event funded by USG and by another USC source
